text:
DKB Recomp

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 DKB Recomp is a static recompilation of Donkey Kong Bananza (Nintendo Switch 2, 2025) into a native Windows
x86-64 application with a Vulkan renderer. There is no emulator at run time: the game's ARM64 code is translated to C
ahead of time and compiled into one executable, and its graphics calls are answered by a host implementation of
NVN 2. It is built on TotK Recomp, which does the same for Tears of
the Kingdom on the original Switch.

As far as we know, no other static recompilation of a Switch 2 game is public.

 [!IMPORTANT]
 No game files are included, and none ever will be. You need your own copy of Donkey Kong Bananza , dumped
 from your own console. Instructions for obtaining those files will not be provided. The game itself is never
 downloadable: the release carries the installer, and
 everyone builds the game from their own dump.

 Status

 Playable on recent NVIDIA cards, well past the first level. Players report runs through layer -101, sublayer 200,
the Glacier layer, Snow World (Layer 500), the Resort and the Tempest layer. The current release is 0.5.2
(24 November): the TOTK to DKB rename of settings and files, the Feast Layer black shards ( 439), 4 GB cards ( 437)
and Switch 2 controllers on USB. The latest release carries
 DKB-Launcher.exe , one small Windows file that installs the build tools, builds the game from your own dump ( .nup ,
 .nx or folders) and updates in place with one click. It also has the setup zip, a Linux AppImage, and a
macOS preview: docs/installer.md.

New in 0.5.2:
- Settings are DKB and files dkb. ; TOTK variables are ignored, and totk.ini is copied to dkb.ini once.
- Fixes for the black shards on the Feast Layer muck ( 439), the missing grass on Linux ( 462), nearly full 4 GB cards
 ( 437) and GPUs that share system memory ( 497).
- Draw merge on by default ( 468), 4 replay threads from 6 logical processors, Switch 2 controllers on USB without
 Steam ( 496), pad background ( 502) and pad shortcuts ( 516).

New in 0.5.0:
- Performance presets ( preset = 1..5 or recommended , F1 menu "Preset") and expected frame rates per hardware tier:
 docs/requirements.md.
- dlss mode picks the DLSS and FSR quality mode by name. The setup can fetch NVIDIA's DLSS DLL or AMD's FSR 4 after
 you accept their licenses.
- Local co-op with a second gamepad as Pauline ( 240), Thai on 3.2.0 ( 180), and 16:10 screens ( 249).
- Prompts follow your button swaps ( 416, 440), and a start-up screen shows progress ( 430).
- Entering a level stalls about half as long on Windows with NVIDIA ( 442).
- 4 to 7 thread CPUs stall less: draws cost about 14% less to record, and level transitions no longer starve the
 replay.
- replay threads is on by default on every discrete AMD card on the proprietary driver.
- Crash fixes: a 1.0.0 banana pickup crash ( 428), a layer-change crash ( 443, 204), and EmeraldRush with
 realtime = 1 ( 411).
- Setup and launcher work: RomFS in place ( 305), the packed shader cache, Uninstall, --set , --play , and every
 cache kept inside the install folder ( 402).

The full list, with credits, is in the release notes. What still fails:

- GPU hangs under RADV on Linux ( 99, 122, 198, 204), and a driver fault on Intel Arc ( 3).
- Black shards where salt, acid or muck meets slime ( 139, 266, 387, 439).
- Guest crashes without a reproduction here ( 126, 148), and a device loss on an RTX 5080 at B1000 ( 336).
- Hitches in the Resort and Tempest layers on 4 GB cards ( 437; preset = 1 or astc bc = 1 ).
- Heavy scenes stay around 40 to 45 fps on CPUs with 4 to 6 threads (docs/dkb-lowend.md).
- Text is soft above 1080p unless scene res = full ( 214).

Earlier releases: 0.4.0 fixed the Snow World and Glacier device loss on NVIDIA and the AMD Windows device loss.
0.4.1 added the FSR 3.1 and FSR 4 upscalers, frame generation, CRT and window filters, and Polish. 0.4.2 cut
stalls in heavy scenes, on first runs and on CPUs with few threads.

RecompLauncher on Linux and macOS: docs/recomp-launcher.md. Progress, day by day: docs/devlog.md. Last updated: 20 November 2026.

 Phase State 
 --- --- --- 
 F0 CPU ✅ main and sdk (180,061 functions) lift with no unsupported instruction (ARMv8.3 pointer authentication and LDAPR added). Differential tests against Unicorn pass. 
 F1 OS ✅ Boots on TotK Recomp's Horizon host with the Switch 2 differences: RomFS, save, audio, controller. 
 F2 NVN 2 ✅ 700 NVN 2 entry points answered; the game loop runs. 51 new command buffer calls (mesh shaders, VRS, DLSS, push constants…) are accepted but not recorded yet. 
 F3 Shaders ✅ All 4,820 Ampere shader stages of the first 3D scene go through Eglantine's Ampere-to-Maxwell lowering and TotK Recomp's translator to SPIR-V. 
 F4 Vulkan ✅ The title screen and the tutorial's 3D scene render. 
 F5 Playable ✅ Controller, guide movies (VP9), push constants, installer and releases 0.1.0 to 0.4.0. 
 F6 Stability 🚧 Device lost on NVIDIA and AMD, RADV hangs and guest crashes in later areas. 
 F7 Performance 🚧 A heavy scene runs at about 58 fps on bananza , with a stall of about 0.45 s on area loads. 
 F8 Image 🚧 Missing effects, some textures and terrain details. 
 F9 Platforms 🚧 Linux and macOS preview packages, RecompLauncher, audio and DLC. 

The plan, phase by phase: docs/bananza-plan.md. What is open right now:
Roadmap to playable.

 How it works

 

The longer version is in docs/architecture.md (shared with TotK Recomp) and
docs/bananza-shaders.md (the NVN 2 shader work).

 How to help

Each open problem is a separate, well-bounded job with its own issue. Pick one, say in the issue that you are on it,
and keep each pull request to one topic. Issues labelled
 in progress are
already taken, and the top of the roadmap says what is
being worked on right now.

 No code needed , only your PC and your own copy of the game:

- 3 Test on your GPU. Everything so far was checked
 on one NVIDIA card. Runs on AMD, Intel and other NVIDIA cards, with logs, show what breaks there.
